glosses: Habitant, citoyen ou personne originaire de Biélorussie.

examples.text: Et puisqu’il n’était pas envisageable de sacrifier de "vrais" Russes, il hésita alors entre quelques ethnies excentrées et minoritaires mises à sa disposition : Ukrainiens, Roumains, Sibériens, Géorgiens, Mongols, Turcs, Azéris, Kazakhs, Tadjiks, Uzbeks, Biélorusses, Arméniens...
Muriel Merolle a vécu, comme peu de passionnés, le sacre inédit de Caroline Garcia, dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, au Masters WTA, contre la Biélorusse Aryna Sabalenka (7-6, 6-4).

verbogen vorm van de stellende trap van Wit-Russisch
kobieta lub dziewczyna narodowości białoruskiej, obywatelka Białorusi, mieszkanka Białorusi

examples.text: Wielu Polaków żeni się z Ukrainkami, Białorusinkami i innymi nie-Polkami.

glosses: женск. к белорус; жительница или уроженка Белоруссии

examples.text: Я понял, что не ошибся… да, это сосед… все разговоры были при нём… История моей жены такая: она из-под Минска, белоруска.

glosses: Forma del femenino singular de bielorruso.
Of or relating to Russians with tsarist or anti-Soviet sympathies in the period directly following the Revolution in 1917.

examples.text: The overseer of the clinic was a White Russian woman, a nun, formerly of the Russian Orthodox community in Jerusalem, but a good-hearted woman. In these cases, we should not be too scrupulous politically, said the priest.

glosses: Of or relating to Belarus, literally \"White Russia\", or its language.
A cocktail consisting of coffee liqueur, vodka, and milk.

examples.text: Few cocktails include milk and cream, so the White Russian is a welcome departure from the norm. Already a popular drink in its own right, the White Russian was made famous by Jeff Bridges’ character in “The Big Lebowski.”

glosses: A White Guardist, a Russian who did not support the Socialists in the Revolution in 1917 and the Russian Civil War (1917–1923), and afterwards (e.g. as a White émigré).

examples.text: The White Guard colony in Harbin is armed and organized along military lines. At the head of this army of counter-revolution—the shock troops of Japanese imperialism—stands the notorious tsarist bandit, "Ataman" Semionov.
